NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to install a thermoelectric heat pump module on the spindle housing to actively remove heat from the bearing region during warmup. Standard practice relies on passive cooling via low-flow coolant; this intervention introduces active cooling via a Peltier device, a departure from the thermal management paradigm. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is spindle cooling jackets, which use fluid circulation; this intervention uses solid-state thermoelectric cooling, avoiding fluid dynamics and enabling localized, rapid heat extraction. The mechanism attacks the failure by directly reducing the bearing temperature rise, thereby minimizing thermal elongation of the spindle shaft.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔL = α·L·ΔT, where ΔL is elongation, α is thermal expansion coefficient (~12×10⁻⁶/°C for steel), L is spindle length, and ΔT is temperature change. A 10°C reduction in bearing temperature (achievable via Peltier cooling) reduces ΔL by 120×10⁻⁶·L. For a 300mm spindle, this cuts elongation by 36μm, well below the 10μm threshold. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = bearing temperature; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 10°C via active heat pumping; this REDUCES the thermal elongation failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (a) Existing spindle housing (no modification), (b) Commercial thermoelectric module (Peltier device, 12V, 50W, ΔT max 60°C, e.g., Laird Technologies TEC1-12706), (b) Standard aluminum heatsink (80mm×80mm×30mm, finned, natural convection), (c) Adjustable DC power supply (set to 8V, 4A during warmup), (c) Timer relay (programmed to activate Peltier for first 20 minutes of warmup). Standard practice: Continuous low-flow coolant (no new parts). Our intervention adds: (b) Thermoelectric module, (b) Heatsink, (c) Power supply adjustment, (c) Timer relay activation.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: 0 new parts, 0 operational loss. Intervention: (b) Thermoelectric module ($25, 1hr install), (b) Heatsink ($15, 30min install), (c) Power supply adjustment (0 cost, 10min setup), (c) Timer relay activation (0 cost, 5min setup). Total burden: $40 hardware, 2.5hr labor (vs. standard practice's 0). Burden class: same (both use existing infrastructure + minor additions). Operational loss: zero (Peltier runs during warmup only, no production impact).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Mount dial indicator on spindle housing, measure displacement at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 minutes after startup with and without intervention. Instruments: Dial indicator (±1μm resolution), thermocouple (bearing housing), stopwatch. Pass/fail: Displacement ≤10μm at all time points with intervention; intervention reduces peak displacement by ≥50% vs. baseline. Duration: 3 cycles (warmup/cooldown). Kill criterion: Displacement exceeds 10μm at any point.
